sections.name: General Knowledge / Current Affairs of India and Goa

p1.title: Passage 1
paras: Yoga, originating in ancient India, is widely regarded as a practice integrating physical postures, breathing techniques, and meditation. Beyond its physical benefits, yoga emphasizes mental discipline, self-awareness, and holistic well-being. In modern contexts, yoga has been commodified, with fitness studios, branded courses, and online tutorials making it a global phenomenon. While such commercialization increases accessibility, it risks reducing yoga to mere exercise, detached from its philosophical and spiritual roots. Scientific studies suggest that consistent practice improves flexibility, cardiovascular health, stress management, and cognitive performance. However, casual adoption without proper guidance may cause physical strain or misinterpretation of principles. Governments and institutions increasingly promote yoga for public health and cultural diplomacy. Consequently, yoga occupies a dual role: as both a therapeutic practice and a symbol of cultural heritage, requiring balance between authenticity and contemporary adaptation.

p2.title: Passage 2
paras: South Indian cuisine, originating from the states of Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh, and Telangana, is distinguished by its diversity, use of spices, and emphasis on rice, lentils, and coconut. Traditional dishes such as idli, dosa, sambar, and rasam are celebrated for their balance of flavor, nutrition, and digestibility. Culinary practices often reflect local agriculture, climate, and cultural rituals, making food a repository of regional identity. Fermentation techniques, like those used in idli and dosa batter, enhance both taste and nutritional value. Coconut, tamarind, and curry leaves are recurring ingredients that provide unique flavor profiles. While globalization has popularized South Indian dishes worldwide, commercialization sometimes alters traditional recipes to suit mass tastes. Despite modernization, home cooking and temple cuisines continue to preserve authenticity. Consequently, South Indian food illustrates a dynamic interplay between tradition, innovation, and cultural continuity.

questions.q: Choose the correct preposition: “She is skilled ____ solving complex problems.”
questions.why: Skilled at + -ing. GPSC CBRT, Mar 2026.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence:
opts: Hardly he had arrived when the phone rang.
Hardly had he arrived when the phone rang.
Hardly he arrived than the phone rang.
Hardly had arrived he when the phone rang.
questions.why: Hardly + had + subject … when. GPSC CBRT, Mar 2026.

questions.q: Identify the relationship shown by the conjunction: “I left early, lest I should miss the train.”
questions.why: 'Lest' means 'in order not to'. GPSC CBRT, Mar 2026.

questions.q: Choose the correct option: “He talks as though he ____ everything.”
questions.why: 'As though' for an unreal present takes the past form. GPSC CBRT, Mar 2026.

questions.q: Choose the one word for: “A person who looks on the bright side of things”
questions.why: An optimist expects good outcomes. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: DILRMP 3.0, whose guidelines were launched in September 2026, concerns:
opts: digital land records, with GIS maps and a universal Bhu-Aadhaar
questions.why: Digital India Land Records Modernization Programme. Sep 2026.

questions.q: The 57th GST Council meeting recommended raising the GST prosecution threshold from ₹1 crore to:
The 27th Asian Table Tennis Championships, where the Indian men's team won bronze, were held in:
World Teachers' Day is observed on:
questions.why: India's own Teachers' Day is 5 September.

questions.q: Which Goan grandmaster received a ₹5 lakh award at the launch of the Goa Chess Academy in July 2026?
questions.why: Launched by CM Pramod Sawant in Panaji, 30 July 2026.

questions.q: India's first indigenously built Fleet Support Ship, launched on 6 October 2026, is named:
questions.why: Built at Hindustan Shipyard Limited, Visakhapatnam.

questions.q: In October 2026 the IMF raised its forecast of India's FY 2026-27 growth to:
questions.why: From 6.4%. Oct 2026.

questions.q: The World Development Report 2026, 'The Promise of Artificial Intelligence', is published by the:
questions.why: Launched in New Delhi on 8 October 2026.

questions.q: The Tenzing Norgay National Adventure Award is India's highest award for:
opts: adventure activities on land, sea and air
questions.why: Awardees for 2024 were announced in September 2026.

questions.q: Gandhi's Dandi March began on 12 March 1930 from:
questions.why: Against the salt tax.

questions.q: The banker's gain on a sum due 2 years hence at 10% a year is ₹24. What is the present worth?
questions.why: BG = TD × RT/100, so TD = 24 × 100 ÷ 20 = 120; PW = TD × 100 ÷ RT = 600. GPSC CBRT, Apr 2024.

questions.q: Chug : Train :: Bang : ?
questions.why: A train chugs; a door bangs (the sound each makes). GPSC CBRT, Apr 2024.

questions.q: Is the average age of a school's students less than 17? I. Class VIII is under 25% of the school. II. Class VIII averages 18 years; the rest average 16.
questions.why: II alone allows any average between 16 and 18. With I, the weight of 18 is under 25%, so the average is below 16.5. GPSC CBRT, Apr 2024.

questions.q: The speeds of a train and a man are 6 : 1. The 650 m train passes a pole in 1 minute 5 seconds. How long will the man take to cross a 240 m platform?
Amit, Anil and Ajit ride the same distance at speeds 5 : 4 : 3, taking 94 minutes in total. How long does Anil take?
questions.why: Times are in the ratio 1/5 : 1/4 : 1/3 = 12 : 15 : 20; 94 ÷ 47 = 2, so Anil 30 min. GPSC CBRT, Apr 2024.

questions.q: In how many ways can the letters of the word LOGICAL be arranged?
questions.why: 7 letters with L twice: 7!/2! = 2520, not listed. GPSC's key said 5040, which ignores the repeated L. GPSC CBRT, Jun 2025.

questions.q: In how many ways can the letters of PENCIL be arranged so that the vowels are always together?
questions.why: Treat E, I as one block: 5! × 2! = 240. GPSC CBRT, Jun 2025.

questions.q: Find the odd term:
questions.why: The others contain only vowels. GPSC CBRT, Jun 2025.

questions.q: Jonathan passes a church one-fifth of the way to the stadium at 6.05 pm and a farm one-third of the way at 6.15 pm. When does he reach the stadium?
questions.why: 1/3 − 1/5 = 2/15 of the way in 10 min, so the whole trip is 75 min. 4/5 left at 6.05 = 60 min: 7.05 pm. GPSC CBRT, Jun 2025.

questions.q: Should competitive examinations for professional courses be fully online? I. Yes, less printing and transport, faster results. II. No, it disadvantages rural and low-income students without reliable internet.
questions.why: Both give real, relevant consequences. GPSC CBRT, Jun 2025.

questions.q: Hahnemann advised (§236) that in intermittent fevers the remedy is best given:
opts: at the height of the chill
immediately or very soon after the paroxysm ends
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. So that it can act before the next paroxysm.

questions.q: Diseases kept up by avoidable noxious influences such as poor diet or bad habits, which disappear when these are corrected, are called by Hahnemann:
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Not true miasmatic diseases.

questions.q: In the sixth edition of the Organon Hahnemann preferred the term:
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Earlier editions said 'vital force' (Lebenskraft).

questions.q: Ill effects of grief with sighing, a lump in the throat, contradictory symptoms and aversion to consolation suggest:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Ignatia: paradoxical symptoms, acute grief.

questions.q: Copious, acrid, excoriating discharge from the nose with bland lachrymation suggests:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Euphrasia is the reverse: bland coryza, acrid tears.

questions.q: Cough excited by the slightest inhalation of cold air, with the patient covering the mouth to breathe warm air, is characteristic of:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Rumex: tickling cough from cold air, covers head.

questions.q: Ulcers with splinter-like pains, offensive urine like horse's urine, and cracks at the mucocutaneous junctions suggest:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Nitric acid: splinter pains, horse-like urine odour.

questions.q: In homoeopathic pharmacy, 'succussion' means:
opts: grinding a drug with sugar of milk
vigorous shaking of a liquid potency with forceful strokes
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. Liquid potencies are made by succussion; insoluble drugs by trituration.

questions.q: The Drugs and Cosmetics Rules require homoeopathic medicines to be manufactured under a licence issued by:
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. Licences are issued by the State Drug Controller (State Licensing Authority).

questions.q: A rubric in a repertory is:
opts: a heading under which remedies producing that symptom are listed
questions.why: Topic 4, Repertory. The basic unit of a repertory.

questions.q: Which repertory follows Kent's plan but is arranged with chapters in alphabetical order?
questions.why: Topic 4, Repertory. Robin Murphy's repertory lists chapters alphabetically.

questions.q: The blood-brain barrier is formed mainly by:
opts: tight junctions of capillary endothelium in the brain
questions.why: Topic 5, Anatomy and Physiology. Supported by astrocyte foot processes.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a function of the liver?
opts: Production of erythropoietin in the adult
Synthesis of clotting factors II, VII, IX and X
questions.why: Topic 5, Anatomy and Physiology. In adults erythropoietin comes mainly from the kidney; the other three are hepatic functions.

questions.q: Dry gangrene usually results from:
questions.why: Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. Wet gangrene involves venous congestion and infection.

questions.q: The Widal test is used in the diagnosis of:
questions.why: Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. Agglutinins to O and H antigens.

questions.q: Measles with fever, profuse bland coryza and burning, acrid lachrymation in a child calls for:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Euphrasia: acrid tears, bland nasal discharge (the reverse of Allium cepa).

questions.q: Bell's palsy affects the:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Lower motor neurone facial palsy.

questions.q: Bilious diarrhoea and stitching right-sided liver pains relieved by lying on the right side, with jaundice, suggest:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Chelidonium: pain under the right scapula, liver remedy.

questions.q: Hyperemesis gravidarum means:
opts: severe, persistent vomiting in pregnancy causing dehydration and weight loss
questions.why: Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. May need hospital care.

questions.q: Under India's UIP, the first dose of measles–rubella (MR) vaccine is given at:
questions.why: Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. Second dose at 16–24 months.

questions.q: A painful hard swelling of the knee in an elderly person, worse after use, with crepitus, most likely indicates:
questions.why: Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. Degenerative joint disease.

questions.q: Inflammation of the conjunctiva with redness and sticky discharge is called:
questions.why: Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. 'Pink eye'.

questions.q: Chlorination of drinking water aims to leave a free residual chlorine of about:
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Ensures continued disinfection.

questions.q: The measure of central tendency most affected by extreme values is the:
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. The median is resistant to outliers.

questions.q: Post-mortem staining (livor mortis, hypostasis) is due to:
opts: gravitational pooling of blood in dependent parts
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Begins within about 1–2 hours of death.
